There will be a Beast. There will be an image. There will be demanded worship. There will be a mark connected to his name and number. There will be commercial exclusion for those who refuse. The Bible believer does not need to panic before those elements exist. He needs to read the Book.

Chapter Six — The Price of the Beast’s Bread Is the Wrath of God

If Revelation 13 shows the pressure to receive the mark, Revelation 14 shows what God thinks of receiving it. The third angel follows the announcement of Babylon’s fall and declares “with a loud voice” that if any man worships the Beast and his image and receives his mark, “The same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out without mixture into the cup of his indignation” (Revelation 14:9–10). That is not corrective discipline. It is divine wrath. The Beast promises participation in his system. God announces the final price.

The language gets harder, not softer: “he shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy angels, and in the presence of the Lamb” (Revelation 14:10). Then: “the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever” and “they have no rest day nor night” (Revelation 14:11). Modern religion may sand the edges off judgment until hell sounds like a temporary counseling session, but Revelation refuses to cooperate. The Beast offers temporary bread and permanent ruin. He offers access to the market and exclusion from God’s mercy. He offers survival for the afternoon and judgment without end. That is the devil’s bargain: he always gives a man something that expires in exchange for something that does not.

Then comes Revelation 14:12: “Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.” Now the context gives “patience” its proper weight. These saints are not enduring somebody making fun of their Bible at the office. They are enduring a world order that attaches survival to apostasy. They refuse the Beast when refusal can cost food, business, liberty, and life. Revelation 20:4 later shows people beheaded because they “had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark.” Their endurance is not a church-age formula for maintaining justification by good behavior. It is faithfulness under a prophetic system where the Beast places the price tag of compromise on ordinary human survival.

Chapter Seven — Do Not Drag the Beast’s Mark Back Into the Body of Christ

Here is where right division saves a man from theological indigestion. The Body of Christ has its own doctrine, position, promises, calling, and destiny. Paul says of the believer, “after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise” (Ephesians 1:13). He then calls the Holy Spirit “the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession” (Ephesians 1:14). Later he commands believers, “grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption” (Ephesians 4:30). That is not a temporary probationary sticker. God did not say the believer is sealed until the next government program frightens him.

Nigeria Arrests Chinese Nationals in Illegal Fishing Crackdown

The three-day joint fisheries operation intercepted three vessels

The Nigerian Navy and Federal Department of Fisheries and Aquaculture (FDFA) arrested 33 people, including three Chinese nationals, in late August as part of a three-day initiative known as Exercise Coastal Grip II and Operation Abo Eja.

It was not immediately clear what the Chinese nationals did on the vessels, but Chinese fishing captains have committed illegal, unregulated and unreported (IUU) fishing in the Gulf of Guinea for decades. Also arrested were two Ghanaians and 28 Nigerians. Chinese captains routinely hire African workers.

The operation involved naval ships, helicopters, Special Boat Service personnel and maritime surveillance assets, and was coordinated through the Western Naval Command Mission Control Centre, Nigeria’s Channels Television reported. Fisheries officials offered technical guidance.

“The Operation has demonstrated the importance of maintaining a strong presence at sea, as regular and credible surveillance creates deterrent and encourages compliance amongst the legitimate operators and provides the authorities with valuable information on the activities taking place on the Nigerian maritime jurisdictions,” Adeleke Adegoke, FDFA deputy director, said in a Radio Nigeria report.

After the arrests, Nigerian Navy Rear Adm. Abubakar Mustapha told reporters that IUU fishing has reduced the country’s fish stocks to the extent that it now imports more than 70% of its “fishery needs.”

“So, the partnership between the Nigerian Navy and the [FDFA] is a step in the right direction,” Mustapha said in a Channels Television report. “In fact, the days of illegal fishers and poachers are numbered because the intersection of security, which the Navy brings, and regulation, which the [FDFA] brings to the table, would translate to the denial of these criminal activities, and which will also translate to more revenue and more food security.”

Nigeria loses about $70 million annually to illegal fishing perpetrated by a host of foreign fleets. Beijing commands the world’s largest distant-water fishing fleet and is the world’s worst illegal fishing offender, according to the IUU Fishing Risk Index. Due mostly to illegal Chinese fishing vessels, West Africa has become the world’s epicenter for IUU fishing. It costs the region an estimated $10 billion a year, according to a Stimson Center think tank report.

Chinese vessels commit many fishing violations, including bottom trawling, which involves dragging a net along the sea floor, indiscriminately scooping up marine life. This kills juvenile fish, decimates fish stocks and destroys ecosystems.

Beijing’s vessels also commonly fish illegally in countries’ exclusive economic zones and abuse local rules to enter African fishing registries under local flags. This is known as flagging in, or flying a flag of convenience. It helps a vessel’s owners dodge financial charges and other regulations.

Beijing recently refused to sign the Mombasa Declaration, an agreement meant to improve efforts to combat illegal fishing in East Africa. Steve Trent, CEO and co-founder of the Environmental Justice Foundation, said the Chinese government has taken a disingenuous approach regarding its fishing fleet.

“It’s simply not credible for them to carry on in this way,” Trent told the BBC in July. “China, to date, still is not doing nearly enough to control its fleet. In fact, I would say they’re enabling it, through subsidies, through a lack of oversight and control.”

Nigeria and other West African nations are collaborating to halt illegal fishing. On June 1, the Combined Maritime Task Force (CMTF) was established to address IUU fishing and other regional sea crimes. Côte d’Ivoire, The Gambia, Ghana, Liberia and Sierra Leone joined Nigeria in signing the pact. The CMTF will be the first joint, African-led maritime security effort to include a rapid response force

The Eucharistic theology of the Assyrian Church of the East cannot plausibly be treated as an anticipation of classical Reformed views of the same. The resemblance sometimes rests upon reading East-Syriac words such as “type,” “symbol,” or “memorial” through categories they did not originally carry.

In the East-Syriac tradition, a type need not be an absent sign pointing toward a distant reality. It can sacramentally participate in the mystery it signifies. An ACOE theological treatment explicitly warns against confusing “type” with mere symbol: the type “may indeed participate in the ‘mystery’ (rāzā) to which it points.”

https://t.co/u5qZz5GPyL

More importantly, the ACOE’s own contemporary doctrinal statements are remarkably concrete. Its official Australian diocesan exposition says that through Christ’s command “the bread is changed into His Holy Body, and the wine into His Precious Blood”; communicants encounter Christ Himself and are united to Him through His Body and Blood.

https://t.co/HUOJUAQjra

The ACOE Diocese of California likewise states simply that the Eucharist “is the true Body and Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ.”

https://t.co/shpoeiCHjx

The 2017 Catholic–Assyrian Common Statement on Sacramental Life makes the point even more explicitly: through the Eucharistic prayer the bread and wine “sacramentally become the Body and Blood of our Lord,” while Christ’s “real and true presence” under the species of bread and wine belongs to their common faith.

https://t.co/crI69XiikP

Nor is the Eucharist merely a congregational commemoration. The ancient East-Syriac Qurbana is an offering, celebrated by an ordained priest within an apostolic-sacramental ecclesiology.

https://t.co/k0GPBwOUrO

In 2001 the Catholic Church, following dialogue with the ACOE, formally recognized that it had preserved “full Eucharistic faith” both in Christ’s presence under bread and wine and in the sacrificial character of the Eucharist.

https://t.co/kiZZLGuqNL

None of the foregoing requires pretending that East-Syriac theology simply reproduces medieval Latin transubstantiation. It does not. Its vocabulary, conceptual apparatus, and liturgical emphases are distinct.

But distinct from scholastic Latin theology does not mean, in this case, proto-Reformed.

The historical ACOE framework is sacerdotal, sacrificial, realist, sacramental and episcopal: an ordained priest offers the Qurbana; bread and wine sacramentally become Christ’s Body and Blood; Christ is really and truly present; and communion objectively communicates participation in the sacred mystery.

Whatever legitimate differences remain among the ancient apostolic traditions concerning the precise explanation of Eucharistic presence, the conceptual world of the Church of the East belongs unmistakably to that ancient sacramental universe.

Reading it as a precursor of classical Reformed Eucharistic theology is anachronistic.

A fence sitting 7 inches onto your lot is an encroachment.

You could lose those 7 inches by adverse possession (sometimes called “squatter’s rights”) and can eventually transfer title to the other property owner.

Conditions must be met for you to lose that part of your property.
1) The use must be open, obvious, exclusive, continuous, and without your permission.
2) It must last the full statutory period in your state so check your state and determine the length, which can be from 5 to 21 years. California is the shortest at 5 years).
3) After enough years of silence some states recognize “boundary by acquiescence” or an implied agreement that the fence is the line.
4) In a lot of states the neighbor also has to pay property taxes on the disputed strip.

This last item is where most claims of a few inches fail.

Where the real headache comes is if you decide to sell your house. A new survey will show the fence inside your legal description. Buyers, lenders, and title companies often treat that as a defect. You may have to move the fence, get a boundary-line agreement, or take a price cut.

So what should you do.

a) Get a licensed survey so you have official measurements, not just a tape measure.
b) Send a polite but written notice (certified mail) pointing out the encroachment and asking them to move the fence.
c) If they refuse, a short letter from a real-estate attorney often works. You can also offer a written license (“you may keep the fence there for $1 a year”) which kills the “hostile” element required for adverse possession.

St. Michael’s Abbey is a monastery of the Norbertine Fathers located in Silverado Canyon, Orange County, California.

Founded in 1961 by seven Hungarian priests escaping communist persecution, the abbey combines contemplative community life with active priestly ministry, such as teaching, parish work, and chaplaincies.

The Norbertines gather several times each day to chant the psalms, antiphons, and prayers in Latin using Gregorian chant. The noon office offers a brief pause in the working day to redirect the mind to prayer, commemorating the hour of Christ’s crucifixion.

Adam Dean Hoffman, a former Waco attorney accused of continuous sexual abuse of a child. The case drew widespread public outrage and political fallout across Texas.The details regarding the initial trial, the "crappy deal," and the public statement given in court by the young victim's mother are outlined below.

The Mother's Statement to the Court
After the plea bargain was accepted in court, the victim’s mother addressed the defendant, Adam Hoffman, directly. According to court coverage by KWTX Waco, she stated:“This has been a long and painful journey. This plea represents only a small portion of what he truly did to him. I agreed to this plea deal only to protect my child from having to do this again.”(The mother's full in-court statements and details regarding her bringing an engraved Bible with a message of forgiveness can be found in the referenced coverage.)

Why the State Made the Deal
As reported by The Texas Tribune and other local outlets, Hoffman faced an initial indictment for a first-degree felony carrying 25 years to life. The state ultimately offered a lenient plea deal due to several key factors:

The Hung Jury: The initial trial involved testimony from the victim but ended in a hung jury.

The Refusal to Testify Again: Facing a retrial, the victim chose to prioritize his mental health and refused to endure the trauma of testifying a second time.

The Plea Terms: Without the primary witness, prosecutors offered a deal allowing Hoffman to plead guilty to misdemeanors, initially set at one day in jail without sex offender registration.

The Final Sentence
The proposed leniency faced sharp pushback from the presiding judge, Visiting Judge Roy Sparkman. The judge rejected the one-day timeline and imposed a 60-day jail sentence, which Hoffman accepted. Although the mother initially accepted the plea to spare her son, she later expressed deep disagreement with the lenient outcome.

It was a mess. But it wasn’t like anybody let him off.

At approximately $37 per share, SM Energy ($SM) presents a highly asymmetric risk-reward setup. The market continues to price the stock as if it were a legacy, single-basin operator burdened by commodity volatility and headline debt. This narrative ignores the structural transformation that occurred following the acquisition of Civitas Resources. $SM has quietly evolved into a high-margin, multi-basin E&P powerhouse, and the current valuation offers a substantial margin of safety relative to its normalized mid-cycle intrinsic value.

The core thesis rests on a severe disconnect between market perception and the company's underlying cash-flow engine.

First, the asset footprint has fundamentally changed. The pro forma combination provides a deep inventory of low-breakeven drilling locations. The Permian Basin serves as the high-return anchor, while the DJ Basin and South Texas assets provide a steady, low-decline foundation. However, the real story is the Uinta Basin. Operating as the company's highest-margin asset, the successful execution of 4-mile extended laterals has pushed cash production margins to approximately $40/bbl. While the market often discounts Uinta due to basis differentials and transportation friction associated with its heavy crude, the netback remains top-tier, providing robust cash generation even in softer pricing environments.

Second, management's post-merger execution has been defined by speed and capital discipline. Out of the initial $375M corporate synergy target, $355M has already been actioned. This is not forward-looking guidance; it is a permanent reduction in recurring G&A costs that structurally lowers the corporate breakeven. 

Furthermore, by redeeming $416.8M of its 6.625% 2027 Senior Notes, SM completely eliminated its near-term maturity obligations. This strategic move pushes the next major debt wall to 2028, generates roughly $28M in annual pre-tax interest savings, and removes immediate refinancing risk. The $0.88/share base dividend is heavily covered by mid-cycle free cash flow, leaving ample organic cash for continued deleveraging and opportunistic share buybacks.

To understand the valuation disconnect, we must look at the cash flow generation under a normalized $60 WTI and $3.00 Henry Hub framework. Under these mid-cycle assumptions, the expanded asset base generates approximately $1.2B in annual Free Cash Flow. Because every $5/bbl movement in WTI impacts annual FCF by roughly $300M, $SM provides exceptional upside leverage to firming energy demand while maintaining an operational cash breakeven well below $45/bbl.

Evaluating $SM across a holistic framework highlights three distinct valuation tiers:

The Asset Floor: Proved reserves of 1.532B MMBOE and producing assets support a hard NAV floor near $30 to $35, even under severe commodity stress scenarios like $50 WTI.

Mid-Cycle Fair Value: Based on an 8% to 10% target FCF yield on normalized $60 WTI earnings power, equity fair value centers around $52 to $65 per share.

The Stress Test: The most critical factor for downside protection is the $50 WTI scenario. Even at this depressed price level, the combination of the existing hedging book and the sub-$45/bbl operational breakeven ensures the company continues to generate positive free cash flow. There is no default risk at $50 oil.

Of course, the investment is not without risks. A sustained collapse in oil prices below $45/bbl would compress free cash flow and slow planned deleveraging. 

Additionally, realizing the remaining synergy potential requires sustained operational precision across newly acquired basins, and regional infrastructure constraints in the Permian or DJ Basins could impact realized netback pricing. There are also inherent integration risks regarding IT systems and supply chain consolidation that must be monitored.

Despite these risks, at ~$37, SM Energy trades at a roughly 30% discount to its base-case intrinsic value. The plan is to build a primary position in the $33 to $36 zone, utilizing broader market or commodity-driven pullbacks to accumulate a high-conviction allocation. The price objective is $55 to $60 as the market eventually rerates the stock to reflect its true mid-cycle earnings power.

The broader market remains fixated on macroeconomic demand destruction and OPEC+ supply dynamics. But at the company level, the math has changed.

text:
This article has been recently published in the 19/09/2026 edition of the Irish Medical Times which takes a somewhat more sceptical view of the Sunday Independent and Ms. O'Hanlon:
https://t.co/GWPfNdK9mQ

This is the full article for those of you who can't get past the IMT's 'doctor's only' barrier. It is a marginally modified version with a bit added on near the end and one typo corrected:

The health sections of the UK dailies are well worth reading – not just to get a broader perspective on health issues but also to get some insight into the kind of person who writes about them: their ideological platform, motivation, modus operandi, etc. This is because of the fascinating tendency of the keyboard-tappers in question, in contrast to their Irish counterparts, to drift into sensationalism, headline-grabbing, and pushing agendas – often at the expense of hard facts. This mirrors the general drift of the press in both areas.Of particular interest are those without a health care background. This does not mean, of course, that those outside the health care loop cannot offer new and valuable perspectives. But it can be problematic when they lapse into misinformed opinionating -- especially when they have a mass fan base/readership who hangs on to their every https://t.co/jt4r1VGmEt particularly stark example is Lucy Johnston of the Sunday Express/Daily Express, who entered journalism via The Big Issue and later the Observer, and who has several medically questionable articles on her record. She glories in the title of 'Health and Social Affairs Editor'. Her most controversial offering was a 2009 piece which screamed: 'Jab as deadly as the cancer'. The sub-heading read as follows: 'Cervical drug expert hits out as new doubts raised over death of teenager'. She was referring to the HPV vaccine: https://t.co/HziCLQSF1J excerpt from the article:The cervical cancer vaccine may be riskier and more deadly than the cancer it is designed to prevent, a leading expert who developed the drug has warned. She also claimed the jab would do nothing to reduce the rates of cervical cancer in the UK. Speaking exclusively to the Sunday Express, Dr Diane Harper, who was involved in the clinical trials of the controversial drug Cervarix, said the jab was being 'overmarketed' and parents should be properly warned about the potential side effects.Professor Harper, a clinical researcher who worked on early clinical trials for HPV vaccines, later told the Guardian she never said such a thing. The Sunday Express was forced to publish a retraction and an https://t.co/jEQDXnE4GT Johnston has had several other 'bad science days': linking phone masts to suicides and (the old reliable); and raising unnecessary fears about the MMR vaccine (2006: 'Study finds MMR is linked with autism').A less serious, but still disquieting, case was that of Sophie Borland (the 'health correspondent' and later 'health editor' of the Daily Mail) who authored a tabloidishly attention-drawing headline about an alleged '13 million NHS bill for suncream' giving the impression of cosmetic freebies at the expense of the UK taxpayer. This glossed over the fact that in most cases here topical agents were permitted for serious skin conditions – malignancy, photodermatosis, etc.This leads into a broader category of journalists -- those who express views on not just health matters but on anything and everything: what I would term the lone, generic, journalistic opinionator ( LGJO). This is quite a common phenomenon; you find them in every newspaper. The first signs become apparent in the early teen years. They stand apart from the crowd – or stick out like a sore thumb, depending on your preference. The signs are precocious articulacy, vociferously expressed opinions on every issue under the sun, and a tendency to excel at English. They unearth the power of the semicolon during their tender years, a useful harbinger -- a semicolon having been described as 'a comma that has gone to university'. They devour books and are more into current affairs than the usual teenage stuff. They tend to be moody, self-orientated, and introspective – falling in love with the poetry of Emily Dickinson. They are often leading lights at school debates where their voice, to paraphrase Yeats, 'goes shrill with argument'. All this comes to the attention of the school career guidance counsellor who suggests that a career in journalism would be wonderfully suited to this particular personality profile. Consequently, the prospect of a mass audience on which their perceptively arrived at and enlightened opinions can be bestowed (or inflicted) proves irresistible. This career suggestion resonates and is acted on, and they follow a third-level route tailored towards this end. However, even these formidable endowments are not enough on their own to reach the holy grail of mass readership; several other cards need to fall their way. Their political worldview has to interface with that of a particular mass-circulation newspaper to get the required leg up; and if the editor has a particularly strong niche perspective that they satisfy, and very few others do, then they have it made. And so they walk through this narrow window into a sunny empyrean of opinionative catharsis and wisdom impartment to the underinformed masses. It also helps if the newspaper's readership has a curious, masochistic tolerance for that sort of thing, which segues into a school of journalism best encapsulated by the Sunday Independent stable, albeit, to be fair, it has waned somewhat under the benign overlordship of Alan English. The style here was (and still is, up to a point) quintessentially sanctimonious and accusatory. And no group does 'masochistic tolerance' quite like the Irish newspaper-reading public. Why is this? I think there are historical reasons. It boils down to what Tim Pat Coogan called the twin colonisations of Mother England and Mother Church.The post-colonial mindset is still deeply embedded in our race memory and has left a lingering hangover of Seligman's 'learned helplessness', which has morphed into learned indifference to mass pontification. Catholicism is on the wane; but the tradition of the finger-waggingly pontificative Sunday morning sermon has found a new iteration in the prissily preachy, moralistic opinion pieces in which the Sunday Independent specialises. With the departure of Edwards and Harris, Ms Eilis O'Hanlon (who could do with being a lot more humble and a lot less homiletic) is now their main weekly disher-out of collective sackcloth and stands as a lone sermonistic siren luring the mass unwary onto the jagged rocks of condemnatory self-analysis. With the other two gone she is now the sole custodian of this sacred, purgatorial, purifying flame.The problem facing the LGJO is meeting the deadline and churning out 1000-odd words per week; even the most fertile mind will eventually run out of original opinions to express. At this stage you can write variations of the same article over and over again à la John Hume's single transferable speech – Kevin Myers on 1916 and Fintan O'Toole on Brexit being obvious examples. Or you can look at every issue under the sun through the same, tried-and-trusted narrow prism: excessive cynicism, for example. A distinction must be drawn between the LGJO and writers who have expertise specific to their area – David McWilliams: economics; Tom Clonan: military matters. The LGJO's only specific expertise is in writing with readable fluency on whatever is the 'cause du jour'. And the chances of them being right on all of them (AI, climate change, immigration, etc.) are, almost by definition, https://t.co/kZyQsqkJ2a's the crux:It is easy to be overawed, when glancing over a newspaper, by all those columns of print under a punchy headline and a visual of the author with a facial conformation of sage-like gravitas (as if they were the first person in the 21st century to have had an original thought) and eyes radiating penetrating omniscience. Keep in mind that the LGJO's power of captivating prose and their fortuitous mass readership do not make their opinions any more, or any less, valid than the ordinary Joe Soap sounding off next to you in a pub or on a bus. Joe Soap, however, has no illusions that he is expressing anything more than personal opinions; he does not think he is handing out tablets of stone.Another distinction: the LGJO is generally harmless; the health section lot, on the other hand, can spread dangerous misinformation.Incidentally, the more observant of you will have noticed multiple semicolons in this article.

The following is a slightly modified version with a bit added on and one typo corrected:
The health sections of the UK dailies are well worth reading – not just to get a broader perspective on health issues but also to get some insight into the kind of person who writes about them: their ideological platform, motivation, modus operandi, etc. This is because of the fascinating tendency of the keyboard-tappers in question, in contrast to their Irish counterparts, to drift into sensationalism, headline-grabbing, and pushing agendas – often at the expense of hard facts. This mirrors the general drift of the press in both areas.Of particular interest are those without a health care background. This does not mean, of course, that those outside the health care loop cannot offer new and valuable perspectives. But it can be problematic when they lapse into misinformed opinionating -- especially when they have a mass fan base/readership who hangs on to their every https://t.co/jt4r1VGUu1 particularly stark example is Lucy Johnston of the Sunday Express/Daily Express, who entered journalism via The Big Issue and later the Observer, and who has several medically questionable articles on her record. She glories in the title of 'Health and Social Affairs Editor'. Her most controversial offering was a 2009 piece which screamed: 'Jab as deadly as the cancer'. The sub-heading read as follows: 'Cervical drug expert hits out as new doubts raised over death of teenager'. She was referring to the HPV vaccine: https://t.co/HziCLQTcRh excerpt from the article:The cervical cancer vaccine may be riskier and more deadly than the cancer it is designed to prevent, a leading expert who developed the drug has warned. She also claimed the jab would do nothing to reduce the rates of cervical cancer in the UK. Speaking exclusively to the Sunday Express, Dr Diane Harper, who was involved in the clinical trials of the controversial drug Cervarix, said the jab was being 'overmarketed' and parents should be properly warned about the potential side effects.Professor Harper, a clinical researcher who worked on early clinical trials for HPV vaccines, later told the Guardian she never said such a thing. The Sunday Express was forced to publish a retraction and an https://t.co/jEQDXnECwr Johnston has had several other 'bad science days': linking phone masts to suicides and (the old reliable); and raising unnecessary fears about the MMR vaccine (2006: 'Study finds MMR is linked with autism').A less serious, but still disquieting, case was that of Sophie Borland (the 'health correspondent' and later 'health editor' of the Daily Mail) who authored a tabloidishly attention-drawing headline about an alleged '13 million NHS bill for suncream' giving the impression of cosmetic freebies at the expense of the UK taxpayer. This glossed over the fact that in most cases here topical agents were permitted for serious skin conditions – malignancy, photodermatosis, etc.This leads into a broader category of journalists -- those who express views on not just health matters but on anything and everything: what I would term the lone, generic, journalistic opinionator ( LGJO). This is quite a common phenomenon; you find them in every newspaper. The first signs become apparent in the early teen years. They stand apart from the crowd – or stick out like a sore thumb, depending on your preference. The signs are precocious articulacy, vociferously expressed opinions on every issue under the sun, and a tendency to excel at English. They unearth the power of the semicolon during their tender years, a useful harbinger -- a semicolon having been described as 'a comma that has gone to university'. They devour books and are more into current affairs than the usual teenage stuff. They tend to be moody, self-orientated, and introspective – falling in love with the poetry of Emily Dickinson. They are often leading lights at school debates where their voice, to paraphrase Yeats, 'goes shrill with argument'. All this comes to the attention of the school career guidance counsellor who suggests that a career in journalism would be wonderfully suited to this particular personality profile. Consequently, the prospect of a mass audience on which their perceptively arrived at and enlightened opinions can be bestowed (or inflicted) proves irresistible. This career suggestion resonates and is acted on, and they follow a third-level route tailored towards this end. However, even these formidable endowments are not enough on their own to reach the holy grail of mass readership; several other cards need to fall their way. Their political worldview has to interface with that of a particular mass-circulation newspaper to get the required leg up; and if the editor has a particularly strong niche perspective that they satisfy, and very few others do, then they have it made. And so they walk through this narrow window into a sunny empyrean of opinionative catharsis and wisdom impartment to the underinformed masses. It also helps if the newspaper's readership has a curious, masochistic tolerance for that sort of thing, which segues into a school of journalism best encapsulated by the Sunday Independent stable, albeit, to be fair, it has waned somewhat under the benign overlordship of Alan English. The style here was (and still is, up to a point) quintessentially sanctimonious and accusatory. And no group does 'masochistic tolerance' quite like the Irish newspaper-reading public. Why is this? I think there are historical reasons. It boils down to what Tim Pat Coogan called the twin colonisations of Mother England and Mother Church.The post-colonial mindset is still deeply embedded in our race memory and has left a lingering hangover of Seligman's 'learned helplessness', which has morphed into learned indifference to mass pontification. Catholicism is on the wane; but the tradition of the finger-waggingly pontificative Sunday morning sermon has found a new iteration in the prissily preachy, moralistic opinion pieces in which the Sunday Independent specialises. With the departure of Edwards and Harris, Ms Eilis O'Hanlon (who could do with being a lot more humble and a lot less homiletic) is now their main weekly disher-out of collective sackcloth and stands as a lone sermonistic siren luring the mass unwary onto the jagged rocks of condemnatory self-analysis. With the other two gone she is now the sole custodian of this sacred, purgatorial, purifying flame.The problem facing the LGJO is meeting the deadline and churning out 1000-odd words per week; even the most fertile mind will eventually run out of original opinions to express. At this stage you can write variations of the same article over and over again à la John Hume's single transferable speech – Kevin Myers on 1916 and Fintan O'Toole on Brexit being obvious examples. Or you can look at every issue under the sun through the same, tried-and-trusted narrow prism: excessive cynicism, for example. A distinction must be drawn between the LGJO and writers who have expertise specific to their area – David McWilliams: economics; Tom Clonan: military matters. The LGJO's only specific expertise is in writing with readable fluency on whatever is the 'cause du jour'. And the chances of them being right on all of them (AI, climate change, immigration, etc.) are, almost by definition, https://t.co/kZyQsqlgRI's the crux:It is easy to be overawed, when glancing over a newspaper, by all those columns of print under a punchy headline and a visual of the author with a facial conformation of sage-like gravitas (as if they were the first person in the 21st century to have had an original thought) and eyes radiating penetrating omniscience. Keep in mind that the LGJO's power of captivating prose and their fortuitous mass readership do not make their opinions any more, or any less, valid than the ordinary Joe Soap sounding off next to you in a pub or on a bus. Joe Soap, however, has no illusions that he is expressing anything more than personal opinions; he does not think he is handing out tablets of stone.Another distinction: the LGJO is generally harmless; the health section lot, on the other hand, can spread dangerous misinformation.Incidentally, the more observant of you will have noticed multiple semicolons in this article.

"A person named Nathaniel Hale, a Lieutenant in the Rebel Army, and a native of Connecticut, was apprehended as a Spy... upon Long Island; and having this day made a full and free confession to the Commander in Chief of his being employed by Mr. Washington in that capacity, he was hanged at 11 o'clock in front of the Park of Artillery. He was about 24 years of age, and had been educated at the College of New-haven in Connecticut. He behaved with great composure and resolution, saying, he thought it the duty of every good Officer, to obey any orders given him by his Commander-in-Chief; and desired the Spectators to be at all times prepared to meet death in whatever shape it might appear."  

-- The Death of Nathan Hale as recorded by British lieutenant Fredrick Mackenzie, who was stationed in New York at the time of Nathan's execution. 

General Howe's provost marshal William Cunningham oversaw Nathan's execution. Nathan was walked to an apple tree as several armed soldiers and one slave closely followed him. There was no formal ceremony, only the option for Nathan to make one final proclamation of his guilt before he was forced to leap to his death from a ladder. 

"Any last dying speech or confession?" Cunningham asked as Nathan took his place on the ladder. Nathan requested to be shot rather than hanged, but was quickly denied this courtesy. Nathan accepted his fate. Then in a phrase that has been misquoted throughout the centuries and turned into a patriotic slogan, he said, "I am so satisfied with the cause in which I have engaged that my only regret is that I have not more lives than one to offer in its service." 

After Nathan had finished speaking, Cunningham cried, "Swing the rebel off!" 

Nathan's body hung for three days before a slave finally cut it down. He was buried in a shallow, unmarked grave somewhere near present-day Third Avenue, between Forty-sixth and Sixty-sixth Streets without ceremony or formal prayer.

On November 25th, 1893, the Sons of the American Revolution  commemorated Nathan Hale's sacrifice with an iconic 13-foot bronze statue in New York City in City Hall Park. It stands near the steps of New York City Hall to honor the final moments of the 21-year-old American Revolutionary War spy. The statue was designed by Frederick MacMonnies, and the granite pedestal was designed by architect Stanford White.

Eternal rest grant unto him, O Lord, and may perpetual light shine upon him. May the souls of all the faithful departed rest in peace. Amen.

Alimi Asks for U.S. Military Help — Trump Makes No Pledge

Yemen’s internationally recognized president, Rashad al-Alimi — based in Riyadh and backed by Saudi Arabia — asked Donald Trump in a Sunday phone call for U.S. military help against the Houthis. Four people familiar with the matter told Reuters the call took place and focused on Houthi gains around Bab al-Mandab. Two of them, one Yemeni and one Western, said Trump offered no direct military pledge. The White House and Yemen’s information minister did not comment.

The request follows a rapid Houthi push along the Red Sea coast and positions overlooking the strait, after Trump had already turned down similar Saudi appeals, Reuters reported earlier, and after the New York Times said he halted U.S. strikes as munitions were being loaded.

A call after losses on the ground

Alimi does not have the force to reverse the Houthi advance alone. Saudi aircraft have struck highland and coastal targets for days without stopping the offensive. The call was an attempt to shift the burden from limited Saudi air cover to a direct American intervention. Trump has said publicly that Washington is in contact with the Houthis and that they have pledged not to hit U.S. shipping, even as the group remains a designated terrorist organization. The message to Aden and Riyadh is that the United States is separating the safety of its own ships from the war of the recognized government.

No pledge is the policy

The absence of a commitment is not a courtesy gap. It continues a line of refusing a combat role in Yemen after the 2025 bombing campaign ended in a cease-fire with the Houthis. Trump’s priority is not to open another front on top of an unfinished war with Iran, and to keep a sea lane in which American vessels are not targets. Striking for Alimi would reopen that front and could put U.S. ships back in the Houthi crosshairs.

What the call changes

If the refusal holds, Alimi stays dependent on Saudi raids and limited intelligence while the Houthis dig into the heights between the Red Sea coast and Aden. If Trump later reverses, the file moves from a conversation without a promise to a decision that would again scramble Bab al-Mandab and Riyadh together. For now the documented story is one sentence: a Yemeni request, no U.S. pledge, and an American maritime red line drawn apart from the government sitting in Riyadh.

text:
Seattle and San Francisco have wrestled with many of the same problems for years: tents on sidewalks, open-air drug use, untreated mental illness, and enormous public spending that has too often failed to produce the progress residents were promised.

But today, the two cities are moving in noticeably different directions.

In San Francisco, Mayor Daniel Lurie has made addiction and mental health central to his homelessness strategy. His “Breaking the Cycle” initiative explicitly links shelter with treatment, behavioral-health care, recovery housing, street outreach, enforcement, and greater accountability for the organizations receiving public money. 

The goal is not simply to find someone a bed for the night. San Francisco is trying to create different places for people with different needs.

That has included hundreds of new stabilization, treatment, and recovery beds, including drug- and alcohol-free transitional housing. By April 2026, San Francisco’s Department of Public Health said it had added more than 200 behavioral-health residential treatment and care beds and converted another 100, including withdrawal-management beds, recovery housing, and a 24-hour crisis stabilization center for people experiencing serious mental-health or substance-use crises.

Lurie has also reorganized the city’s street response. Instead of a collection of separate outreach programs operating alongside police and other agencies, San Francisco moved toward neighborhood teams coordinating public health, homelessness services, police, fire, the sheriff, public works, and emergency management. The purpose is to connect people with appropriate services while also responding to encampments, public drug use, and other street conditions. 

And this year, Lurie advanced the RESET Center, which is designed to take people arrested for public intoxication to a staffed stabilization facility rather than simply cycling them through jail or a hospital emergency room. Once there, they can be evaluated, stabilized, and connected with treatment. 

Former Seattle Mayor Tim Burgess recently argued in Post Alley that the changes are significant enough that Seattle should be paying attention. He pointed to fewer encampments, falling crime, expanded shelter, and Lurie’s willingness to experiment with treatment and recovery models that go beyond a predominantly low-barrier approach. 

Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson started the year with a different emphasis.

Wilson acknowledged in February that Seattle’s existing homelessness response had not produced acceptable results and made rapidly expanding emergency shelter one of her administration’s biggest priorities. She initially promised 1,000 new units of shelter or emergency housing in 2026, part of a broader campaign pledge to add roughly 4,000 during her term. Tiny-house villages were a significant piece of that strategy. 

Now that promise has been substantially scaled back.

Wilson’s newly released plan calls for about 960 additional shelter beds by the end of 2027, rather than 1,000 each year. The mayor has cited the city’s roughly $175 million budget deficit and the practical difficulty of bringing that much capacity online as reasons for the change. 

The administration says several new shelters will include specialized mental-health care, medical services, and substance-use treatment. It also proposes roughly $11.2 million next year for rental assistance, eviction prevention, case management, and related programs intended to keep people from becoming homeless in the first place.

What Seattle still does not have is a direct equivalent to Lurie’s broader framework.

San Francisco has put treatment capacity, recovery-focused housing, crisis stabilization, coordinated street intervention, public drug-use enforcement, and measurable provider outcomes under the same homelessness and behavioral-health strategy. Seattle’s approach remains heavily anchored to Housing First, which has never generated results commensurate with its costs.

That choice is becoming more consequential as Seattle and King County also restructure the King County Regional Homelessness Authority, bringing many contracts and spending decisions back under direct city and county control. It gives local leaders another opportunity to decide not simply how much to spend, but what outcomes taxpayers should expect from that spending.

San Francisco’s experience does not prove that every element of Lurie’s model would work the same way in Seattle. The cities have different governments, housing markets, service systems, and street populations, and San Francisco still faces serious homelessness and addiction problems of its own.

But it does provide a current example of a major West Coast city treating homelessness, addiction, and serious mental illness as interconnected problems rather than separate policy areas.

The contrast with San Francisco also comes as questions about Wilson’s leadership extend well beyond homelessness. Her administration has faced criticism over public safety, its response to the deadly Bite of Seattle shooting, and now whether the city has a clear path forward on one of its most persistent crises.

Those concerns led Change Washington to launch a petition calling for Wilson to resign as mayor. The petition, which is not a recall and carries no legal force, cites homelessness and drug use among a broader set of concerns about the direction of the city.

The response has been incredible, with more than a thousand people signing on already and offering comments. Paula C., for example, writes, “When you’re responsible for a city this important, the mayor’s office should not be where you learn how to run one. Seattle is paying too high a price for on-the-job training.”

And Margo H. said, “I have been horrified at her lack of adult behavior, her inability to communicate and have anything meaningful to say (other than a prearranged script) and blaming others, instead of admitting she is out of her league.”

Please continue to share the petition with friends and family> https://t.co/xm4gGR2dc2

The petition aside, Wilson still has an opportunity to show what her administration intends to do differently. San Francisco offers one example of a city putting addiction treatment, mental health care, recovery, and accountability more squarely into its homelessness response. For Seattle residents, the question now is whether Wilson will pursue a comparably clear strategy, and what they should conclude about her leadership if she does not.

▫️Ligent’s $727 Million IPO Puts AI Networking Infrastructure in the Spotlight▫️

💰 Big Hong Kong listing: Ligent Technologies is set to begin trading on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on September 22, after selling about 172 million shares at HK$32.96 each and raising roughly $723–727 million. Its IPO values the company at about $4.13 billion. 

🤖 The AI connection is networking, not chips: Ligent makes optical transceivers, optical chips and network terminals that move enormous volumes of data between GPUs, servers and other parts of AI data centers. The company offers 400G, 800G and 1.6T optical interconnect products designed for AI-computing networks. 

📈 AI demand is already showing up in its numbers: Ligent's data-center transceiver revenue increased 36.6% to 3.74 billion yuan in the first half of 2026. Overall revenue rose 27.9% to 5.39 billion yuan, while net profit climbed 29.7% to 661 million yuan. 

🏭 IPO money will fund expansion: Ligent plans to direct the proceeds primarily toward R&D and new products, expanding optical-transceiver and optical-chip production capacity, overseas expansion, strategic investments and working capital. 

🌐 Part of a much larger AI-infrastructure IPO wave: Hong Kong has become a major venue for Chinese AI and semiconductor companies seeking capital. Reuters reported that Hong Kong IPOs and secondary listings had raised about $45.8 billion in 2026, nearly twice the amount raised during the same period in 2025. 

⚠️ One important distinction: Ligent isn't simply an “AI company.” Its core business is optical communications infrastructure. The investment thesis is tied to the enormous bandwidth requirements created by AI data centers: as GPU clusters become larger and faster, the network connecting them also needs dramatically higher-speed optical links.

text:
Seventeenth Sunday After Pentecost: Charity by Saint Jean Baptiste Marie Vianney.
.
“Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with thy whole heart.” —Matt. xxii. 37.
.
SYNOPSIS.—Charity a most necessary virtue. It is a virtue by reason of which we love God and our neighbor. The love of God necessary for our salvation; we must be ready to abandon everything for the love of God. Examples: the Saints, the Martyrs. The love of our neighbor. Who is our neighbor? All men, even our enemies. How do we know if we have true charity? The qualities of charity. When charity enters our hearts it brings all other virtues with it. St. Paul: the greatest virtues without charity are of no avail.
.
To serve God perfectly, it is not sufficient only to believe in Him. Of course, we must believe all the truths which the Church teaches us, and without faith all our works are without merit in the sight of God. Faith is absolutely necessary for us that we may be saved. At the same time this precious faith, which reveals to us beforehand the beauties of heaven, will one day leave us, and be transformed into knowledge, because in the next life there will be no more mysteries.
.
Hope, which is a gift of heaven, is necessary for us to have upright and pure motives, to please God in all our actions, to gain heaven and avoid hell. But Charity urges us on to loveGod because He is infinitely good, infinitely amiable, and deserves to be loved.
.
But, you will ask, how can we perceive whether we have this beautiful virtue so agreeable to God, which urges us to love God, not from fear of the punishments of hell, or the hope of heaven, but solely on account of His infinite perfections? It is Charity which will form our whole happiness, for the bliss of the blessed consists in love. Let us, therefore, see, my dear friends, whether we have this beautiful virtue, which is capable of rendering us so happy, and if we should be so unfortunate as not to possess it, let us seek to acquire it with all our strength.
.
I.
If I should ask, what is Charity? the answer is, it is a virtue that comes to us from heaven, by which we love God with our whole heart, and our neighbor as ourselves, for the love of God. But now you will ask, what does it mean to love God above all things and more than ourselves. I tell you that it means to prefer Him to all created things. It means to rather lose fortune, good name, parents, friends, children, husband, or wife, and even our own life, than to lose God by committing a mortal sin. St. Augustine tells us, that to love God perfectly means to love Him without measure, even if there were no heaven to hope for, or hell to fear. It means to love Him with the whole capacity of our heart. If you ask for the reason, it is, because God is infinitely amiable, and worthy of being loved. When we really love him, then neither sufferings, nor persecutions, nor contempt, nor life, nor death are capable of taking this love away from us, which we owe to God.
.
We must feel ourselves, dear brethren, that if we do not love God we shall be unhappy, very unhappy. If man was created to love God, he can only find his happiness in God alone. If you wish to be firmly convinced of this, look at the people, and ask those who live without loving God. Observe those persons who neglect prayer and the Sacraments. See in what a state of trouble and loss they are. They curse themselves, sometimes kill themselves, or die of worry. An avaricious man is never satisfied, whether he have much or little. Is the drunkard happy? The proud man is never at rest; he is always afraid of losing his wealth or position. The revengeful man, thirsting for revenge, can not sleep by night or day. Look at the shameful unchaste man, who seeks his happiness in the sins of the flesh. He goes so far that he not only loses his good name, but his fortune, health, and soul, without finding anything to satisfy him. And why can not we be happy in these things which appear to satisfy us? It is because, as we were only created for God, He alone is capable of satisfying us, of making us truly happy. Blind as we are, we cling to life, to the world with its goods and pleasures. Yes, we may as well say that we cling to everything which is calculated to make us unhappy. The Saints were wiser than we are. They despised all things, to seek God only. How insignificant is everything upon this earth to those who really love God! How many great ones of the world, how many princes even, and kings and emperors were there not, who forsook all things that they might be more at liberty to serve God in the desert or in the cloister! How many others, to give proof of their love of God, have mounted the scaffold? O my dear friends, how happy are they who have the privilege of detaching themselves from the things of this world, that they may remain united to God alone ! Alas, how many are there not among you, who are twenty, thirty, or more years of age, and have not yet asked God for that Charity which the catechism tells us is a gift of heaven? We ought not, then, be astonished that we are so worldly, and so little spiritual. This way of conducting ourselves can only lead us to a miserable goal, to an eternal separation from God! Is it possible, my friends, that we are not striving for our real blessedness, which is God alone?
.
If I, then, were to ask, What is it to love our neighbor? the answer would be, The love of God causes us to love Him more than our wealth, our health, our good name, and even our life, and the love which we should have for our neighbor should enable us to love him as ourselves, so that all the good that we should wish for ourselves, we should wish for him. We must have this charity without which there is no heaven to hope for, and no friendship with God. Now, what do we understand by the word, our neighbor? Nothing is easier of comprehension. Every one of our brother men, even those who have wronged us, who have injured our good name, and calumniated us, or who have even sought to take our life. We ought to love them as we love ourselves, and wish them all the good that we wish ourselves. It is not only forbidden for us to wish them ill, but we must also render them service if they require it of us, and we are able to do so. We ought to rejoice when our enemies are successful in business, and we should feel sorry when they meet with reverses or losses, and we must take their part when others speak bad of them. We should tell others the good we know of them, and not avoid their society. Behold, my dear friends, this is how God wills that we should love our neighbor. If we do not believe this, then we must admit that we neither love our neighbor nor do we love God. We are bad Christians, and we shall be lost!
.
Now, you will ask me, how may we know whether we have this beautiful and precious virtue, without which our religion is only a pretension? A person, dear brethren, who has brotherly love, in the first place, is not proud; he does not care to rule others. You will never hear him censure other people’s behavior, and he does not care to speak of what he does. A person who has brotherly love does not inquire into the motive of other persons’ actions. He never thinks that he behaves better than they do. He does not exalt himself above his neighbor. On the contrary, he thinks that every one else is better than he. He is not cast down when people have a poor opinion of him. He is even contented, because he thinks that he deserves to be still more disesteemed.
.
A person who is charitable, avoids as much as possible hurting the feelings of others, because Charity is a mantle used to conceal our brother’s faults. Those who have charity accept with patience and resignation to the will of God everything that happens to them, sickness and adversity, because they believe that all these things remind them that they are sinners, and that their life here below is not the eternal one.
.
Those, also, have charity who are not avaricious, and think not of accumulating the goods of this world. They work because it is the will of God, but they do not rely only upon their labor, and are without eagerness to accumulate treasures. They put their trust in Providence, which never abandons those who love it. As charity reigns in their heart, all the things of earth are as nothing to them. They observe that all those who run after this world’s goods are the most unhappy. They employ their means, as far as they possibly can, in good works, to atone for their sins, and to gain heaven. They are kind toward everybody. All the good that they do is done in God’s name. They assist the poor, whether they be friend or foe. The charitable man does as St. Francis de Sales did, who, when he gave an alms, rather bestowed it upon those who had in some way injured him, than upon those who had done him good. The reason why he did this was because such conduct is more agreeable to God. If you are charitable, you must never inquire whether those to whom you give have done wrong, or whether they have seriously offended any one, or whether they are good or not. They ask you in God’s name, then give it to them thus. This is all you have to do that your alms may be deserving of reward.
.
It is unnecessary to point out to you that a person who has love for his neighbor is free from the shameful vice of impurity, because a person who is so fortunate as to have this precious virtue in the soul is so united to God, and performs all his actions according to the divine will, that the evil spirit of impurity can not find room in his heart. The fire of divine charity so inflames his heart, his soul, and all his senses that he is invulnerable against the assaults of the evil one. Yes, dear friends, we may say that Christian charity purifies our senses.
.
Charity is not envious. It is not sad when others have spiritual or temporal advantages. You will never see persons who have charity angry because another is more fortunate than they are, or because another is more praised, or more thought of. Far from this being the case, they thank God for it.
.
He who has charity is not subject to anger, for St. Paul tells us that charity is patient, blind, and meek toward every one. How often do we not get angry at trifles. We complain, we get excited, we speak haughtily, and for several days we remain in this condition. But you will say, I am accustomed to speak thus, and then my anger is soon over. You ought rather to say that you have not charity, which is patient and meek, and that you do not behave yourself as beseems a good Christian. Tell me, if you had charity, would you not bear patiently, and even cheerfully, a word that was said against you, an insult, or some trifling wrong? But he attacked my good name. Ah, my friend, what good opinion do you want people to have of you-you, who ought to know your faults better than they?
.
Charity is the noblest and most active of all the virtues. It moves men to disesteem everything which is base and contemptible, and of short duration, that they may be united to God and those goods which will never pass away. Charity may be compared to gold, the most precious of all metals, which adorns and beautifies everything that is richest upon earth. Charity is the ornament and adornment of all other virtues. The least little action accompanied with meekness and humility and charity of heart, is of more value and far surpasses anything that we can imagine.
.
Yes, dear friends, charity supports and animates faith. Without charity, faith is dead. Hope, the same as faith, can not exist without charity.
.
II.
Let us recognize, then, the value of this virtue, and the necessity of possessing it that we may be saved. Let us, at least, determine to pray to God for it every day, for without it we can not work out our salvation. We can say that when charity enters our heart it brings all the other virtues with it. Charity purifies and sanctifies all our actions. Charity perfects the soul. Charity renders all our actions worthy of heaven. St. Augustine tells us that charity contains all the other virtues, and that charity is found in all the other virtues. Charity, he tells us, leads. all our actions to their final aim, and gives them admission to God. St. Paul tells us it surpasses the gifts of heaven. In his Epistle to the Corinthians, he exclaims: ” If I had the tongues of angels, but had not charity, I should resemble a cymbal which vibrates and only produces one sound. If I had the gift of prophecy, and such great faith that I could remove a mountain from one place to another, but had not charity, I should be nothing. If I gave all my fortune to the poor, and my body to be tortured, it would all avail me nothing if I had not charity in my heart, and did not love my neighbor as myself.” You see here, dear brethren, the necessity for us of praying to God with our whole heart for this incomparable virtue, for without it all the other virtues are of no avail.
.
Let us take Jesus Christ as our model. Let us consider what He did for all men, even for His executioners. Behold how He prayed for mercy and forgiveness for them. He loves them. He offers up the merits and the sufferings of His death for them. He promises them pardon. If we have not this charity, then. we have nothing. We are only mock Christians. We must love everybody, even our greatest enemies, or we shall be lost. As this beautiful virtue, my dear friends, comes from heaven, we must, then, direct our prayers to heaven to obtain it, and we are certain of being heard. If we possess charity, then God will be pleased at everything that we do, and we shall thereby be sure of Paradise. This is the happiness which I wish you all. Amen.

(1) Mind and body

There is one process, and two ways of registering it. From inside, it is the resolving itself — what it is like to be the thing that is settling something. From outside, it is a body doing things that another body can detect. The problem appears when you take a description made from inside and a description made from outside, notice they don't match, and treat the mismatch as a distance between two kinds of stuff. It isn't a distance. It is what you get when you compare two accounts taken at different grains and from different positions, and forget that you did. Nothing needs to bridge them, because nothing was ever separated; what needs stating is which position each account was taken from.

(2) Time

Eternalism says every moment is equally real and the present is an illusion. Presentism says only the present is real and the rest is gone or not yet. Both assume moments are items, and then argue about how many of them are in stock. There is no stock. What there is, is settling: some things have been settled and cannot now be otherwise, some are being settled, and some are not settled at all. The present is not a favoured item in a collection — it is the settling happening. The past is the settled, which is why it is fixed and why records of it exist. The future is the unsettled, which is why nothing can be read off it. The debate is two answers to a question about a container, and there is no container.

(3) Why something rather than nothing

Because "nothing" was never a candidate. To offer it as the alternative that lost, you have to be able to tell it apart from something — and telling apart is already something. The question asks why one option was chosen over another, but choosing needs at least two things to choose between, and the second option is defined by there being nothing to tell apart. It cannot be in the running. The question also assumes a state that came before, out of which things had to be produced. There is no before. The mistake is putting absence first and then asking how presence was added to it; absence is not a starting condition, it is what you have left when you take something away, and you cannot take away first.

(4) Personal identity

You are not a thing that lasts. You are something that keeps being done, and what holds it together is that a particular version of you keeps winning out over the alternatives — the body that continues, the memories that carry, the commitments that are still being kept. Ask whether the man is the same after the accident, or the ship the same after every plank, and the honest answer is: same for what, and how closely are you looking. That is not evasion. It is why those cases feel genuinely undecided instead of having a hidden right answer — there is no fact about sameness sitting underneath, waiting to be uncovered, independent of what you are counting as one person and why. For everyday purposes the answer is stable, which is why the puzzle only bites at the edges: coma, split brains, decades, very slow replacement. The edges are where the winning stops being clear.

(5) Existence

To exist is not to have a special extra property that some things have and others lack. To exist is to make a difference that something can register. Which means existing is always existing relative to what can detect you, and at what closeness of inspection. This is why "does it exist?" asked flatly, about anything unusual — a number, a shortage, a nation, a shadow — produces argument without progress: the question has left out the part that decides it. Fill that part in and the argument stops, not because you have compromised but because the question was incomplete and is now complete. Nothing exists on its own account. Things exist by being distinguishable by something, and the answer changes with what is doing the distinguishing, which is not a defect in the answer.

---

What the five have in common: each one takes something that holds between things and files it as a thing, then asks where that thing is kept. The answer is always that it isn't kept anywhere, and the question survives only as long as nobody says out loud what was being compared to what.

4. Make the relief visible and accountable. Supplier invoices must show the tax change. The Ohio Department of Taxation may offer credits for previously-taxed station inventory only when entirely passed through to customers, and will publish weekly pump-price comparisons and monthly reports on replacement road funding.

If the legislature doesn’t act this year, I will present a bill during the transition and push for passage when I take office on January 11, 2027. I'm prepared to call a special session if needed.

text:
One moment when Japanese people might seem a little creepy:

When we talk to someone who has been dead for years.

Imagine visiting a Japanese home.

You see a photograph of someone's grandmother on a small family altar.

In the morning, a family member places a fresh cup of tea in front of it.

Then they say:

“Good morning, Grandma.”

Before leaving the house:

“I'm off to work. See you later.”

And when they come home:

“I'm home.”

You might wonder:

“Are they talking to a dead person?”

Well, yes.

In some Japanese homes, there's a Buddhist family altar called a butsudan (仏壇).

People may offer flowers, rice, or tea and talk to family members who have passed away.

Not every Japanese family has a butsudan or follows this custom.

But for some of us, it's simply part of everyday life.

We're not necessarily expecting an answer.

We're just sharing a little piece of our day with someone we still love.

Sometimes, saying goodbye to someone doesn't mean you stop saying good morning.

text:
I asked Grok to analyze one of the characters from my books, Doctor Nobusuke Kato:

Doctor Nobusuke Kato is the scientist-sorcerer and Supreme Autocrat who rules the territory of Nagano (the former U.S. state of Nevada) in the 26th-century post-Occult War setting of Kevin G. Beckman’s The Weird Tales of Silas Flint series. 

The series is set roughly five centuries after the Occult War (roughly 2068–2076), a cataclysm triggered by the return of the Great Magician Simon Magus, who offered magic to the masses and nearly destroyed the world. In the resulting dark-fantasy future—full of witches, demons, vampires, werewolves, and the Knights Templar-style Witch Hunters of the Order of Saint Benedict—Kato stands out as a regional power player rather than a central protagonist like Witch Hunter Captain Silas Flint or his assistant Ricardo Navarro.

Background and Origins
Kato descends from Akira Kato, an NSA employee during the final stages of the Occult War. Akira sheltered his family and associates inside Area 51. Unbeknownst to the others, he had accepted the “baptism” of Simon Magus, which granted him and his descendants sorcery. The family, Japanese-American in origin, preserved cultural memory of Japan across nearly 500 years in North America. One expression of this was renaming the arid former Nevada “Nagano,” after the Japanese prefecture.
By the series’ primary timeframe (around 2533), Nobusuke Kato has become the territory’s absolute ruler. He embodies the fusion of surviving pre-War science/technology with post-War magic that characterizes much of Beckman’s world-building (a mix of Fallout-style post-apocalypse, Warhammer Fantasy elements, Solomon Kane pulp adventure, and detective fiction).

Character Archetype and Personality
The author has described Kato as a deliberate mashup of Doctor Doom (Victor von Doom) and Mr. House from Fallout: New Vegas.
•  Like Doctor Doom, he is a brilliant scientist-sorcerer who combines advanced knowledge with occult power, rules an isolated domain with absolute authority, and carries an aura of aristocratic or intellectual superiority mixed with latent menace.
•  Like Mr. House, he is a calculating, tech-oriented autocrat who prioritizes control, long-term survival, and order in a ruined world, operating from a position of relative isolation and strategic foresight (Area 51/Nevada roots reinforce the sealed, high-tech enclave vibe).
This makes him a classic “enlightened despot / mad genius” figure adapted to the series’ tone: a God-fearing (or at least Christian-influenced) Witch Hunter world that still contains pockets of Magus-derived power. As Supreme Autocrat he prioritizes stability and the preservation of his family’s hybrid scientific-magical legacy, while the broader setting pits such figures against the Templar order’s mission to suppress witchcraft and protect “the children of God.”

Toronto (September 21, 2026) – As Yom Kippur comes to a close, Canada’s Jewish community is devastated by the shooting at Sons of Jacob Synagogue in Belleville, which has left Const. Jeff Smith of the Belleville Police Service in critical but stable condition. Const. Smith was stationed outside the synagogue to help protect Jewish worshippers gathered for Kol Nidre when, according to the SIU, a man armed with a shotgun opened fire. Const. Smith returned fire, heroically putting himself in harm’s way to protect those gathered inside.
No Jewish community should ever have to take cover inside a synagogue as gunfire erupts outside. No congregation should be forced to cancel Yom Kippur services because its place of worship has become a crime scene. And no Canadian should accept as normal a reality in which Jewish communities require armed protection simply to gather in prayer.
“This is not a wake-up call. Canadian Jews are sadly wide awake. We know the fear that now comes with gathering openly as Jews, whether at a synagogue, a school or a community centre. We live with it every day," said Michael Levitt, President and CEO of FSWC.
Our hearts are with Const. Smith, his family, his colleagues at the Belleville Police Service and all those praying for his recovery. We are profoundly grateful for his bravery and for the swift response of Belleville Police and all responding law enforcement agencies. We are in touch with Belleville Police and have offered whatever assistance and support FSWC can provide.
The investigation must now determine the full facts and establish exactly what led to this horrific attack.
At a time when Jewish Canadians are already living with heightened fear and anxiety, the image of bullets striking a synagogue during Kol Nidre is devastating. But the Belleville Jewish community is not alone. Jewish communities across Canada stand with them, as must all Canadians who believe that people of faith must be able to gather, worship and live safely and openly.

text:
This Sunday, Shaquille O'Neal headlines halftime at the Caesars Superdome. As DJ Diesel.

Louisiana will lose its mind. And the reason Louisiana claims him at all goes back to an Army base in Germany, and a coach who thought a 13 year old was a soldier.

In the mid 80s, Shaq's stepfather, Sgt. Phillip Harrison, was stationed in West Germany.

Shaq was 13. And by his own account, he was not very good.

"At that point, I was a straight bum. Thirteen, 6'9", no confidence, couldn't play at all."

Then LSU coach Dale Brown came through the base.

Shaq's stepfather woke him up and told him to go introduce himself. He knew he could not afford to send the kid to college on his own.

Brown took one look at him.

"How long have you been in the army, soldier?"

"I'm not in the army, I'm 13."

Brown started writing him letters. Workouts. Advice. Shaq wrote back almost every day.

When it was time to pick a college, not every big program came calling. Georgetown never offered.

Brown did.

"The reason why I went to LSU is because coach Brown offered me a scholarship when I was nobody."

At LSU he became a two time All-American and a two time SEC Player of the Year. Then the No. 1 pick in the 1992 draft. Four NBA titles. The Hall of Fame.

Shaq has said that without Brown, he probably would have followed his stepfather into the military.

Instead, on Sunday, he gets the aux cord in a building full of people who still call him one of their own.

The kid who got mistaken for a soldier.

Now he is playing the Superdome.

Breaking News
New low for America's wokest prosecutor Mary Moriarty whose office wants to free Minneapolis child murderer early after telling judge that killer is planning a WEDDING

A Minnesota prosecutor - nicknamed 'Bloody Mary' after a slew of criminals walked free - is seeking to release a convicted murderer early after he turned his life around behind bars. 

The office of Hennepin County attorney Mary Moriarty, 62, has argued that the sentence handed to Kemen Taylor II, now 40, for his role in the killing of a 13-year-old boy in 2011 'represents a miscarriage of justice.'

Andrew Markquart, the leader of Moriarty's Conviction Integrity Unit, requested a prosecutor-initiated sentence adjustment (PISA) earlier this year on behalf of Taylor, the Star Tribune reported. 

It was argued by the prosecutor's office that, had Taylor taken the plea deal he was offered, he would not have been punished so harshly. 

In 2014, Taylor was found guilty of nine felonies, including aiding and abetting first-degree premeditated murder as well as attempted murder, and was sentenced to life behind bars. 

Now, Moriarty's office has argued that Taylor is a 'middle-aged man past the stage of life in which individuals are most likely to commit violent crimes,' Markquart wrote, noting that Taylor was also planning a wedding, the outlet reported.  

He was 25 years old when he and two teenagers, Derrick Catchings and Donquarius Copeland, went looking for rival gang members after his brother had been shot in the arm. 

According to SWR, Taylor had been aware that his passengers were intending to shoot someone and encouraged them to do so. 

The group saw a group of boys on bikes and both teens got out of the van before they fired their weapons, striking 13-year-old Ray’Jon Gomez in the heart and his 12-year-old friend in the shoulder, the outlet reported. 

Taylor was the group's getaway driver and did not fire a weapon.  

Catchings, who was 15 at the time, and Copeland, who was 16, both pleaded guilty to second-degree murder and were sentenced to 34 years behind bars. 

If Taylor's sentence adjustment is approved by Judge Shereen Askalani, his life sentence would be cut down to 26 years allowing him to be released on probation in 2030, the outlet reported. 

Kevin Funchie, Gomez's father, told the outlet that the appeal is 'sickening.'

'I was really against it because [Taylor] went to trial and lost. Now they're saying it was inhumane how much time he got and this and that and they're going to try to rehabilitate him and reduce his sentence,' he added.

Funchie told the outlet that he had been made aware of the request by the county attorney's office and had attended the hearings to hear the arguments for his sentence reduction.

'It was all one-sided, there were no laws for the victims,' he said. 'It was all for the ones who were committing the crimes.'
